annotations.text:
Three directions for the sign-in page.

All three use the real tokens: brand #4145c8, ink #172037, canvas #f5f6fa, lines #d9deeb, 7px button radius, 6px inputs, the 10px/1.6px eyebrow, and the system font stack (no webfont is downloaded today).

Pick one and I'll build it properly — desktop, phone and the error/loading states.

A — Living graph wall

Keeps today's 45/55 split and the 01/02/03 lines, but draws the product instead of only describing it: the dark panel carries a quiet node-and-edge motif in the graph kind colours.

Why: it is the one piece of imagery that is honestly about this product.

Tradeoff: the most conservative of the three. If the current page already feels dated, this refines rather than answers that.

B — Centred minimal

No pitch, no split. The app's own canvas colour, one card, a 3px brand edge.

Why: people who open an internal tool already know what it is. This is the fastest path to the field, and the cheapest to keep correct.

Tradeoff: says nothing. If this page is ever shown to a prospect or a new client team, it does no work for you.

C — Editorial

The brand tint floods the page, the statement is set at poster scale, and the card breaks the grid rather than sitting in it.

Why: the most voice, and the most memorable — same palette, far more confidence.

Tradeoff: 86px type needs the copy to stay short, and the offset card is the most fragile of the three at narrow widths.
